title: Rust gateway forwards multicast across backbone; BR multicast drop (spec 04 6.3.4) missing
description: Spec 04-network.md 6.3.4: Border routers MUST NOT forward mesh multicasts to the internet; multicast dropped in both directions (mesh→internet and internet→mesh) unless explicitly configured multicast peering. Classification: divergent (stack split). Evidence: C implemented+tested — lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/router.c:576-589 drops backbone-ingress multicast unless packet->multicast_peering (router.h:146); test lichen/tests/routing_dispatch/src/main.c:277-284. Python implemented+tested — python/src/lichen/routing/router.py:493-499 (is_border_router + is_multicast + not multicast_peering_enabled → DROP), 8 tests python/tests/routing/test_router.py:469-597. Rust gateway MISSING the filter: upstream_to_mesh (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1539-1558) checks only ULA 0xfd then is_local_mesh — a multicast destination falls through to transmit_ipv6_wire (:1556), so internet→mesh multicast is transmitted onto the LoRa mesh; forward_mesh_to_upstream (rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs:914-956) TUN-writes non-local destinations including multicast, so mesh→internet multicast reaches the backbone; the RPL stack accepts multicast destinations as deliverable (rust/lichen-node/src/stack.rs:587-595, 795-806). No multicast_peering or 6.3.4 reference under rust/. Suggested placement: add 0xff multicast drop to upstream_to_mesh and forward_mesh_to_upstream with a multicast_peering config flag mirroring C router.h:146; add gateway end_to_end tests for both directions. Sweep ref R-04-007.
